qs.q: In a study of dimorphic fungal pathogens, researchers observe the colonial morphology at different temperatures. At what temperature do most dimorphic fungi typically express their filamentous mold form versus their yeast form?
qs.e: Most dimorphic fungi grow as molds at ambient room temperature (~23°C) and convert to yeast forms at body temperature (~37°C). Reversing these temperatures fails to match standard pathogenic behavior.

qs.q: Which statement accurately describes a fundamental metabolic characteristic of true fungi compared to plants?
o: Fungi are heterotrophic and lack chlorophyll
Fungi possess chloroplasts for energy production
qs.e: Fungi are strictly heterotrophic organisms that lack chlorophyll and are never photosynthetic. Plants rely on photosynthesis, a process completely absent in the fungal kingdom.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases — Medical: MCQs

qs.q: Fungi that completely lack a known sexual reproductive stage are formally classified under which group?
qs.e: Fungi with no known teleomorph or sexual stage are classified as Fungi Imperfecti, also known as mitosporic fungi. Other groups like Ascomycota and Basidiomycota possess defined sexual stages.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following cellular components is found within the plasma membrane of most fungi and serves as the primary target for polyene and azole antifungal medications?
qs.e: Ergosterol is the major sterol found in the fungal cell membrane, acting as the structural analog to cholesterol in human cells and the main target for antifungals. Chitin and keratin are structural components of the cell wall and hair/nails, respectively.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases: MCQs

qs.q: Which fungal group contains the largest phylum of known fungi and accounts for roughly 85% of human pathogens?
qs.e: Ascomycetes form the largest phylum, comprising over 60% of known fungi and about 85% of human pathogens. Zygomycetes and Basidiomycetes represent smaller portions of human pathogens.
qs.s: Medical Fungi: Classification, Morphology, Reproduction & Spores: MCQs

qs.q: A laboratory identifies a fungus that currently lacks any demonstrated sexual stage and places it temporarily among the 'Fungi Imperfecti'. What is the official taxonomic designation for this group?
qs.e: Deuteromycetes are known as 'Fungi Imperfecti' because they have no known or demonstrated sexual cycle. Once a sexual stage is discovered, they are reclassified into groups like Ascomycetes.
qs.s: Medical Fungi: Classification, Morphology, Reproduction & Spores: MCQs

qs.q: A student is studying the sexual reproduction of fungi and notes that a specific group forms large, thick-walled spores when the tips of two sexually compatible hyphae fuse. Which group does this describe?
qs.e: Zygomycetes produce zygospores through the fusion of compatible hyphal tips. Ascomycetes produce ascospores in asci, and Basidiomycetes produce basidiospores in basidia.
qs.s: Medical Fungi: Classification, Morphology, Reproduction & Spores: MCQs

qs.q: Which fungal phylum is known as the 'Fungi Imperfecti' because no sexual stage has been demonstrated for its members?
qs.e: Deuteromycota are called Fungi Imperfecti because they lack a known sexual cycle. Ascomycota, Basidiomycota, and Zygomycota all have defined sexual spore stages.
qs.s: Medical Fungi: Classification, Morphology, Reproduction & Spores: MCQs
